question: All three vertices of \(\bigtriangleup ABC\) lie on the parabola defined by \(y=x^2,\) with \(A\) at the origin and \(\overline{BC}\) parallel to the \(x\)-axis. The area of the triangle is \(64.\) What is the length of \(BC?\)
solution:
Because \(BC\) is horizontal, its endpoints have the same \(y\)-coordinate. On \(y=x^2\), two distinct points at the same height have opposite \(x\)-coordinates. Thus, exchanging the names \(B\) and \(C\) if necessary, we can write
\[
B=(-t,t^2),\qquad C=(t,t^2),\qquad t>0.
\]
The base \(BC\) has length \(2t\). Since \(A=(0,0)\), the perpendicular height to this horizontal base is \(t^2\). Therefore,
\[
64=\frac12(2t)(t^2)=t^3.
\]
The positive solution is \(t=4\), so \(BC=2t=8\), choice C.
